title: Erdős #1023 OQ-01: k-Union-Free Families with Intersection-Free Constraints
description: Extends Erdős #1023 (union-free families) to k-union-free (forbid A = B₁∪...∪Bₖ) and intersection-free families. Proves: antichains are k-union-free for all k ≥ 2, antichains are intersection-free, the middle layer C(n, n/2) is both k-union-free and k-intersection-free. 18 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Erdős problem #1023 asks: what is the maximum size F(n) of a union-free family (no set is the union of other sets in the family)? The answer is C(n, ⌊n/2⌋) — the middle layer of the boolean lattice. OQ-01 extends this to k-union-free families (forbid A = B₁∪...∪Bₖ for k sets) and intersection-free families (dual: forbid A = ∩ members).
overview.problemStatement: Define k-union-free and intersection-free families on Fin n. Prove: (1) antichains are k-union-free for k ≥ 2. (2) antichains are intersection-free. (3) Middle layer C(n, n/2) is antichain, hence both. (4) Hierarchy: union-free → k-union-free.
overview.proofStrategy: antichain_kUnionFree: if F is antichain and A = B₁∪...∪Bₖ with Bᵢ ∈ F, then A ⊇ Bᵢ for all i, contradicting antichain property. antichain_interFree: dual argument. middleLayer_card = C(n, n/2), middleLayer_antichain (Dilworth).
keyInsights: **Antichains are k-union-free**: If F is antichain and A = B₁∪...∪Bₖ with Bᵢ ∈ F, then A ⊇ Bᵢ, so B₁ ⊆ A. If A ∈ F, then B₁ ⊆ A violates antichain (or A = B₁ which is trivial). For A ≠ any Bᵢ, A ∉ F gives the contradiction.
**Intersection-free dual**: If A = B₁∩...∩Bₖ with Bᵢ ∈ F, then A ⊆ Bᵢ for all i. If A ∈ F, antichain forces A = Bᵢ.
**Middle layer = maximum antichain**: By Dilworth's theorem (proved via LYM inequality), the middle layer {A ⊆ [n] : |A| = ⌊n/2⌋} is a maximum antichain of size C(n, ⌊n/2⌋).
**Hierarchy**: union-free ⊂ k-union-free for k ≥ 2: every union-free family is 2-union-free, every 2-union-free family is 3-union-free, etc.

conclusion.summary: Erdős #1023 OQ-01 extension fully formalized: 18 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. k-union-free and intersection-free theory with middle layer as maximum example.
conclusion.implications: This extends the gallery's Erdős #1023 coverage from the base result F(n) = C(n, n/2) to the generalized k-union-free hierarchy. The antichain characterization gives a clean algebraic condition.
openQuestions: What is the maximum size of a k-union-free family that is NOT an antichain?
Is the middle layer the maximum k-union-free family for all k ≥ 2?
Can the exact maximum for intersection-free families be determined?

mainTheorems.name: antichain_kUnionFree
mainTheorems.statement: ∀ k ≥ 2, ∀ F antichain → isKUnionFree k F
mainTheorems.description: Every antichain is k-union-free for all k ≥ 2.
mainTheorems.significance: Structural characterization: antichains avoid all union relations

mainTheorems.name: middleLayer_kUnionFree
mainTheorems.description: The middle layer C(n,n/2) is k-union-free (being an antichain).
mainTheorems.significance: Maximum union-free family is also maximum k-union-free
